description.x: Sketch the outline of every different tree shape you can find near the school, or on a field trip. Draw the whole tree, not the leaves. Get real variety: something broad, something narrow, something twisted, something that has clearly been cut back to keep it off the wires. Label each sketch with the shape of its crown and, where you can, the name of the species. If you find a tree that has been uprooted, or one whose roots are exposed by erosion or a broken footpath, draw the roots as well. They are usually a surprise.

discussion.x: Which of the trees you drew has the advantage in each of these? Answer from the shape you drew, not from memory.
heavy snow, on a hillside in the Himalaya.
strong pre-monsoon wind, and then a long summer drought.
deep shade, under a bigger tree.
